courseTraceability.rationale: Sustainability Essentials I The course teaches Uses planetary boundaries to introduce scientific tools for understanding sustainability and human impacts on Earth systems. Students interpret graphs and uncertainty, build simple dynamic models, and learn chemical, thermodynamic and mechanical principles relevant to environmental processes. Topics connect climate, ocean acidification, nutrient cycles, energy and materials. An iterative laboratory project makes starch-based biopolymers and measures their strength and elasticity to improve the formulation. Its specific physical, environmental, spatial, research or governance content implements the Earth-society question; contingent project methods remain contingent.. It implements the explicit academic basis “Interdisciplinary natural and social inquiry into scientific and societal questions” and “Mathematical, computational and physical-science reasoning” and “Research design, evidence, scientific argument and interdisciplinary collaboration”.

courseTraceability.rationale: Introduction to Economics The course teaches Introduces microeconomic principles and short-run macroeconomic analysis. The microeconomic component examines supply and demand, strategic interaction, consumer choice, production, costs and competitive markets. The macroeconomic component introduces output, unemployment and inflation, then relates goods and financial markets through the IS-LM model. Students use algebra and graphs to explain economic behaviour and apply models to economic issues. Its economic/institutional decision process or specific research method supports the evidenced science-society/organisational inquiry; no dedicated urban-economics syllabus is inferred.. It implements the explicit academic basis “Interdisciplinary natural and social inquiry into scientific and societal questions” and “Cognition, states, institutions and social behaviour” and “Research design, evidence, scientific argument and interdisciplinary collaboration”.

courseTraceability.rationale: Research in a Sustainable Delta The course teaches Provides a research-project setting for sustainability questions supplied by organizations and companies in the Zeeland delta. Small teams work with an external advisor to review literature, formulate a research question, plan and execute an investigation, and develop a final product, design or report. The substantive topic and practical techniques depend on the partner project; the common focus is an evidence-based research process and engagement with external stakeholders. Its specific physical, environmental, spatial, research or governance content implements the Earth-society question; contingent project methods remain contingent.. It implements the explicit academic basis “Interdisciplinary natural and social inquiry into scientific and societal questions” and “Research design, evidence, scientific argument and interdisciplinary collaboration”.

Reflective inquiries and a final project critically assess sustainability campaigns, identify greenwashing and communicate evidence-based improvements to a public audience. Its specific physical, environmental, spatial, research or governance content implements the Earth-society question; contingent project methods remain contingent.. Students study operationalization, measurement quality, sampling, surveys and experimental and nonexperimental designs, then descriptive statistics, estimation, hypothesis testing and introductory regression. R and R Commander support data display and analysis. Project teams develop instruments and a research plan, collect and analyze data, and report results under explicit research-ethics and privacy requirements. Its economic/institutional decision process or specific research method supports the evidenced science-society/organisational inquiry; no dedicated urban-economics syllabus is inferred.. courseTraceability.rationale: Modern Sociology The course teaches Examines twentieth-century and contemporary social theory alongside critical accounts of modernity, colonialism and disciplinary exclusion. Functionalism, critical theory, Black feminist thought, phenomenology, symbolic interactionism and Bourdieu's work are read with postcolonial, decolonial and Indigenous perspectives. Students compare theories and apply them to empirical cases, including visual material. An individual research paper develops a theoretically grounded interpretation of a selected social phenomenon. This directly contributes institutional/social or historical inquiry, or a specific empirical/source method. No unspecified regional case or invented historical outline is assumed.. courseTraceability.rationale: Dynamic Earth The course teaches Introduces Earth science by linking surface geology to deep-Earth and geophysical processes. Students study rocks, minerals, sedimentation, deformation, stratigraphy, plate tectonics, seismology, the mantle and core, and interactions with climate and other Earth systems. Field and practical work teaches observation and measurement, rock and mineral identification, and reconstruction of geological history. An Ardennes field investigation produces a geological cross-section, stratigraphic column and interpretive report. Its specific physical, environmental, spatial, research or governance content implements the Earth-society question; contingent project methods remain contingent.. courseTraceability.rationale: Living with Water The course teaches Examines how delta societies manage water risks and opportunities, using Zeeland as a central case. Physical and ecological challenges such as flooding, salinization, freshwater scarcity, subsidence and pollution are connected to infrastructure, history, governance, law and justice. Students evaluate engineered and nature-based responses, considering trade-offs and long-term consequences. Site-based inquiry and a project apply these concepts to context-sensitive adaptation in a delta region. Its specific physical, environmental, spatial, research or governance content implements the Earth-society question; contingent project methods remain contingent.. courseTraceability.rationale: Energy & Sustainability The course teaches Studies renewable-energy resources, conversion technologies and their integration into sustainable energy systems. courseTraceability.rationale: Econometrics The course teaches Econometrics supplies tools to analyze data to answer questions of causality and prediction. In this course you learn three estimators—Ordinary Least Squares, Generalized Least Squares, and Instrumental Variables—and three tests—t-test, F-test, and LM-test. Understanding the basic rules of econometrics, particularly the sampling distribution concept, is key, and the course uses Monte Carlo simulations in Stata to visualize it. Tools are applied to estimate economic relationships and make predictions, and students write an empirical paper. Its economic/institutional decision process or specific research method supports the evidenced science-society/organisational inquiry; no dedicated urban-economics syllabus is inferred.. comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both teach practical Python programming, algorithms, code structure and debugging. UvA additionally integrates AI-and-society argumentation; other UCR teaching addresses that separately.

Both directly develop matrices, eigenmethods and discrete/dynamic-system modelling. This covers part of the MathematicsB variant; it does not reproduce the full calculus/differential-equation syllabus.

Both use numerical simulation and mathematical models of changing systems. This is a relationship in a specific primary method; UCR does not reproduce the dedicated philosophical/history-of-emergence and cross-domain case syllabus.
Both examine states, political institutions and human collective life through social-scientific theories and empirical cases. UvA includes a broader anthropology/psychology/sociology framing.

Both investigate sustainability problems through stakeholder evidence, policy/options appraisal and advice. UCR governance advice is not the complete circular-economy consultancy/client project or supply-chain syllabus.
Both directly study neural systems, cognition and human behaviour using psychological and neuroscientific evidence. The complete UvA cognition/microscopy syllabus and weight differ.

Both require teams to formulate and investigate a question, use evidence and communicate research. UCR works on partner-supplied sustainability questions; the full UvA multidisciplinary integration sequence and symposium differ.

Both teach empirical research design, sampling, statistical analysis and practical research. The UvA mixed-methods course also teaches Atlas.ti thematic analysis; this row does not claim its full qualitative/quantitative package.
The integrated cosmology, relativity, quantum/atomic and molecular/evolutionary life-origin inquiry is not reproduced by general environmental science or programming; retain the gap.
Dedicated philosophy of science, demarcation, paradigms and situated knowledge are not reproduced by ethics or philosophy of mind alone.
The specific urban/economic-geography and Amsterdam field-research formation is not replaced by generic economics, social theory or regional environmental context.
Dedicated analysis of disciplinary grounding, common ground and integration in interdisciplinary research is not reproduced by general research skills or PPD.

audience.programmeDescription: Natural and Social Sciences (Bèta-gamma) combines natural and social sciences at the University of Amsterdam. Students study a common first year, then specialise in a major while continuing interdisciplinary project work.
audience.comparisonExplanation: This qualified comparison assesses 69 EC of Bèta-gamma’s common natural- and social-science curriculum, including Projects 1–3 with the illustrated mathematics and consultancy choices. The UCR programmes offer different combinations of Earth and society, responsible computing, or cognition and institutions. They do not reproduce all natural-science, urban, philosophy-of-science or interdisciplinary-project formation. Later major study, Project 4, final research and complete progression are excluded.

curriculum.limitation: All 174 documented EC remain visible. Only the 69 EC common curriculum is assessed.
